surface.entry: Gateway.execute on an isolated PostgreSQL 64711 cluster with a seeded tenant and the authenticated HTTP approval workflow
surface.capability: Synthetic reviewed external write (provider MCP, risk SHARED_WRITE, supportsIdempotency true)
surface.providerBehavior: Persists one durable business object per provider idempotency key in the outbox and reads it back to VERIFIED
surface.approval: approveViaApi over the real API route, CSRF check and one-time decision

behavior.replay: Six executions of the same approved action with identical arguments all return the recorded OK/VERIFIED provider receipt while the adapter is invoked exactly once.
behavior.singleObject: Exactly one external object, one VERIFIED ledger row, one consumed approval and one consumed tool call exist after the initial execution and six replays.
behavior.stableKey: The provider receives the same key as the ledger's logical_action_key, derived from the run, capability and reviewed args hash rather than regenerated per request.
behavior.differentArgs: An execution with a different argument value becomes a separate action that requires its own approval and cannot reuse the prior provider key; no second external object is created.

cases: replaying the same approved action reuses one provider idempotency key and one external object
a different argument set is a separate action and cannot reuse the prior approval or provider key

isolation.note: Original 90 project files plus the approved added files; the new T118 file is listed in approvedAddedFiles.

mutationCheck.mutation: packages/gateway/src/index.ts: replace the stable args hash inside the logical action key with a fresh random UUID per request
mutationCheck.observed: Both tests fail: a replay no longer resolves to the approved action and returns NEEDS_APPROVAL instead of the recorded OK/VERIFIED result.

requirementsFull.note: 36 R items remain IN_PROGRESS and 13 catalog cases remain NOT_RUN; T118 is no longer among the errors (previously 50).

notProven: The synthetic provider is not a real upstream system; no real provider idempotency header or duplicate-suppression behavior was exercised.
No live DingTalk, GLM, DWS or company-MCP request was made.
The test does not certify crash recovery between provider commit and ledger write beyond the existing synthetic checkpoint oracles.
T118 remains NOT_RUN and R31 remains IN_PROGRESS; live acceptance remains BLOCKED_EXTERNAL.
